solutionSql:
SELECT d.shipment_id, COUNT(*)::int AS distinct_scans
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT sc.shipment_id, sc.status, sc.occurred_at
  FROM staging_scans AS sc
  JOIN shipments AS s ON s.id = sc.shipment_id
  WHERE sc.status IS NOT NULL
) AS d
GROUP BY d.shipment_id
ORDER BY d.shipment_id;

ambiguities.phrase: Count the distinct scans of each shipment
ambiguities.readingChosen: Only shipments with at least one counted scan appear (shipments whose only scans have no status, e.g. 33, 86, 167 on the sample, are omitted).
ambiguities.alternativeReading: Every shipment in staging_scans (or in shipments) appears, with distinct_scans 0 when none of its scans count.

ambiguities.phrase: two scans are the same when they have the same status and occurred_at
ambiguities.readingChosen: A scan with a status but NULL occurred_at still counts, and two such scans with the same status are one scan (SELECT DISTINCT treats NULLs as equal).
ambiguities.alternativeReading: A scan with NULL occurred_at is not counted (as COUNT(DISTINCT status || occurred_at) would do), or each NULL-time scan counts separately.

notes: Join to shipments drops orphan and NULL shipment ids; WHERE status IS NOT NULL drops statusless scans; SELECT DISTINCT on (shipment_id, status, occurred_at) removes repeats; COUNT(*) cast to int. Sample: 41 scans, 5 orphans, 3 statusless, one exact repeat (120) gives 32 rows, all count 1. Main doubt is whether zero-count shipments should appear.
superseded: Instruction text changed to state that a shipment with no scan left to count does not appear; re-solved blind by a fresh agent.
